issues.description: Problem statement/UML requires a static method `SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)`, but the solution implements the delivery logic under a different method name `receiveDelivery(String, int, int)`. Students following the statement will implement/call `acceptSupplyDelivery`, which will not match the provided reference solution API and can cause test failures if tests expect the documented method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename `receiveDelivery` to `acceptSupplyDelivery` and keep it `public static`, or add `public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)` as a delegating wrapper calling `receiveDelivery(...)`.

issues.description: Problem statement asks for a static method `acceptSupplyDelivery(...)`, but the provided (commented) Main code calls `shop.acceptSupplyDelivery(...)` (instance-style) and the solution does not provide `acceptSupplyDelivery` at all. Even though calling a static method via an instance compiles in Java, this combination (missing method + instance-style call in the template) is misleading and can block students when they try to run Main or mirror its usage.
issues.suggestedFix: After adding/renaming the method to `acceptSupplyDelivery`, update Main to call it in the documented static form: `SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...)` (or adjust the statement to allow instance-style if intended).
